Same shape as sc-46 but within one document. Anyone quoting an institution's '2027 increase' must say which of the two.

part_b_soft_connections.nature: comparative claim whose arithmetic does not reproduce from the two sections' own tables
part_b_soft_connections.notes: From the 2027 EXPENDITURE totals the CoR is 24.23% less than the EESC (138 750 785 vs 183 122 221), or 26.06% less than the EESC's request. NOT a contradiction - the claim says 'under the current MFF', i.e. 2021-2027 as a whole, and only 2027 figures are in hand. It is a claim whose basis is unstated and uncheckable from these documents. Per Research.1.md 3 both numbers go in and neither is picked. The 'exact same number of Members' limb IS consistent: SEC07 states 329 elected representatives and 329 alternates.

part_b_soft_connections.to: Member States (as obligated parties) - table numbers, subjects and deadlines
part_b_soft_connections.nature: AGENCY ONLY at scale - a binding obligation naming tables and time limits, not publications
part_b_soft_connections.strength: n/a - documented absence, and the scored refutation of G.19 finding 6
part_b_soft_connections.notes: The Regulation describes its own annex as 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit'. The table overview has four columns - number, subject, deadline, period - and no column for a publication or publisher. SECOND independent chain to stop at AGENCY ONLY, after Annex XI (sc-59). Assessed from staged records, not from Annex B as enacted.

part_b_soft_connections.from: Destatis EDP inventory (German government accounts transmission)
part_b_soft_connections.nature: a national statistical office describes its own transmission by naming ten table numbers and no national publication
part_b_soft_connections.notes: The strongest test of the G.19 finding 6 prediction and the cleanest failure. If a member state were ever going to name its own releases this is the record where it would have happened.

part_b_soft_connections.from: Eurostat dissemination products NAMA, NAMQ, NASA, NASQ, GovQ, GovD&D, NA-Pen, BoP, MUFA
part_b_soft_connections.to: Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 (ESA 2010) as stated legal basis
part_b_soft_connections.nature: named products with stable codes, stated cadences and a named legal basis - three of Research.1.md 4's conditions in one table
part_b_soft_connections.strength: Strong; NOT importable until the record is split
part_b_soft_connections.notes: THE COUNTERWEIGHT, reported per Research.1.md 3 because it cuts the other way - but these are Eurostat's OWN products, not member-state releases, so it points the same way as sc-59 rather than rescuing the prediction. The record bundles NINE products under one heading, the exact failure Research.1.md 6 describes; split it into nine before building anything on it. Most node-shaped material in the Eurostat staging area.

part_b_soft_connections.to: the ECB, as collector and re-transmitter
part_b_soft_connections.nature: terminus - reached via an intermediary that publishes nothing of its own
part_b_soft_connections.notes: Kind: redistributed. First clean instance of that terminus kind in the EU branch. Research.1.md 4 defines it as 'reached via an intermediary that publishes nothing of its own - a data vendor republishing someone else's series'; the ECB here plays that structural role for MUFA.

part_b_soft_connections.to: Table 29 of the ESA 2010 Transmission Programme
part_b_soft_connections.nature: the only place in the corpus where a NAMED PRODUCT is tied to a SPECIFIC Annex B table
part_b_soft_connections.strength: Strong as a lead; single instance
part_b_soft_connections.notes: If a table-to-publication mapping exists anywhere in the ESA framework, this is the thread to pull. Everything else in the transmission-programme material runs table-number-to-obligation. Logged as cheap check 5 in G.24.

part_b_soft_connections.to: financial accounts by sector (Deutsche Bundesbank)
part_b_soft_connections.nature: named as the compiler of a component the national accounts bridge to
part_b_soft_connections.strength: Strong as to the naming; target not researched
part_b_soft_connections.notes: 'They also serve as an important instrument ensuring coherence in the system of national accounts as well as bridge to the financial accounts by sector, which the Deutsche Bundesbank (German Central Bank) is responsible for compiling.' Named independently a second time in the QNA source lists ('Balance of Payments Statistics (Deutsche Bundesbank)', 'Monetary statistics of the Deutsche Bundesbank'). A national central bank feeding the national accounts is the same shape as the Bank of Canada material already in the corpus. Obvious second German node.

part_b_soft_connections.to: the German source statistics it names, by title AND EVAS register number
part_b_soft_connections.nature: a document naming its own inputs in a structured list — Research.1.md 7's strongest evidence class
part_b_soft_connections.strength: Strong; a whole sub-graph, not one edge
part_b_soft_connections.evidence: de-destatis-national-accounts.json _dropped (deferred); GNI and QNA inventory source records
part_b_soft_connections.notes: Named inputs include Microcensus; Structural statistics in trade and services (EVAS 47410); Building and housing census (EVAS 31211); Employment statistics (EVAS 13111) of the Federal Employment Agency; monthly statistics of retail trade (EVAS 45212); International trade in goods statistics (ITGS); Cost structure survey (EVAS 42251); VAT statistics. Register numbers make these unusually citable. destatis.de is fully reachable from this environment. Priority F2 in G.26.

part_b_soft_connections.from: ESA 2010 methods and sources for the German GNI (Destatis)
part_b_soft_connections.to: its own publication cadence
part_b_soft_connections.nature: DOCUMENTED CONFLICT — the publisher declares the document non-recurring while the document names its own predecessor
part_b_soft_connections.evidence: destatis-gni.pdf colophon; its section 1.2 heading; the Destatis landing page
part_b_soft_connections.notes: Colophon: 'Periodicity: non-recurring' (published March 2026), which is Research.1.md 4.2's exact disqualifier. But section 1.2 is headed 'Revisions policy and major revisions since the 2021 inventory' and the landing page carries 'Older editions'. A 2021 and a 2025 edition demonstrably exist, four years apart. Likely reading: 'non-recurring' is a per-publication metadata label meaning 'not a scheduled series release'. If the other end accepts that, releases_per_year 0.25 is what the observed interval supports. The QNA inventory is weaker still — no periodicity statement at all.

part_b_soft_connections.nature: DOCUMENTED NON-DEPENDENCY — Research.1.md 5a agreement language, quoted so the link stops being re-proposed
part_b_soft_connections.strength: n/a — a non-dependency, and 5a says it is worth as much as an edge
part_b_soft_connections.notes: 'The ESA 2010 is consistent with the worldwide guidelines on national accounting set out in the System of National Accounts 2008 (2008 SNA)' (Annex A, ch. 1, para 1.05). 'Consistent with' is verbatim on 5a's watchlist. Two further records say it the same way. This link was re-proposed as 'near-certain' during the G.25 wrap and refuted the next session — which is precisely the recurrence 5a predicts.

part_b_soft_connections.from: EU instruments (Annex XI, ESA 2010 Annex B)
part_b_soft_connections.to: member-state publications
part_b_soft_connections.nature: THE BRANCH'S CENTRAL ASYMMETRY — obligation runs downward, naming runs upward
part_b_soft_connections.strength: Three supports; two negative, one positive
part_b_soft_connections.notes: Two binding EU instruments name no member-state publication (three AGENCY ONLYs in Annex XI; table numbers and deadlines only in Annex B). But Germany names ESA 2010 as the legal basis of its own national accounts, in structured metadata with a periodicity beside it. So the obligation is real and binding; what is missing is NAMING, and only in one direction. EU/slices/README.md framed the branch as testing whether the Canada/US zero-cross-border-edges result generalises. Forming answer: neither quite — the EU has the obligation the CA/US pair lacks, and still does not name across the boundary.
